html:
From 1847 to 1874 about 125,000 Chinese men were shipped to Cuba under eight year contracts to work on sugar estates and railways. Many were tricked or kidnapped in southern China.

Planters used them alongside enslaved Africans as the slave trade came under pressure. Conditions were brutal and many died on the voyage or in the fields. A Chinese commission sent in 1874 found such abuse that the trade was stopped.

Many Chinese fought for Cuban independence in the Ten Years' War. Havana's Barrio Chino became one of the largest Chinatowns in Latin America. The coolie trade echoed the Indian indenture in the British islands, as the sugar industry looked for new workers.
